ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: On the left side of the figure are a transformer, bridge rectifier, and filter capacitor, and on the right side is a series voltage-regulator circuit. Transistor VT1 can be seen in the figure; its emitter connects downward to Zener diode VZ, then connects to the lower negative bus; the base of VT1 is horizontally connected to the adjustable sliding terminal node on the right, namely the U_B1 node required in the problem. Then reason: Zener diode VZ stabilizes the emitter of VT1 at 5.3 V relative to the negative bus. Given that the transistor base-emitter voltage U_BE = 0.7 V, the base voltage should therefore be 0.7 V higher than the emitter. So U_B1 = V_Z + U_BE = 5.3 + 0.7 = 6.0 V.

method.method_draft: First inspect the image: identify VT1, trace its emitter down to the Zener diode VZ and then to the negative rail, and trace its base to the adjustable wiper node whose voltage is U_B1. Then use the given Zener voltage and base-emitter voltage: the Zener holds VT1 emitter at 5.3 V relative to the negative rail, and the base must be 0.7 V above the emitter. Therefore U_B1 = 5.3 V + 0.7 V = 6 V.

method.method_draft: First inspect the image: locate the right-side divider R1–Rp–R2 connected between the output rails, with the Rp wiper connected to the base of VT1. With the slider at the midpoint, split Rp into 250 Ω above and 250 Ω below the wiper, giving equal total resistance above and below the wiper because R1 = R2 = 1 kΩ. Thus the wiper/base voltage is the sampled feedback node. In regulation, VT1 conducts when its base is one base-emitter drop above its Zener-held emitter, so the feedback node must be V_Z + U_BE. Substitute the text values: U_B1 = 5.3 + 0.7 = 6 V.
